lastPlanConflicts.why: R11 acceptance requires the project's start-up check (app-boots) to be enabled so that it runs scripts/smoke/run.mjs and to pass for this feature, and the design states that creating scripts/smoke/run.mjs is what switches app-boots on. But app-boots is a fixed command check (kind: command) that only echoes 'Not set up in this project ... no scripts/smoke/run.mjs' and exits 78; it never invokes the runner and does no file detection. The engine itself reports it as 'could not run (not set up in this project yet: devteam adopt doctor can set it up)', and the adoption baseline says enabling it needs a separate 'devteam run ...' plus 'devteam adopt refresh'. Adding the file from inside the feature therefore does not enable the check, and enabling it is outside the design's scope (SCOPE-001) and the pack guidance even says not to create the harness. The acceptance line can never be met as written, so BOOT-001 remains unproven; either the requirement must drop the claim that app-boots runs the runner and passes (accept it relaxed/unproven), or the builder must enable the check separately.

findings.description: The smoke runner mutates the real user data directory. R11's edge case requires the runner to change no real data or project files whether it passes or fails, but it opens the real `~/.shipright/builds.db`, marks real Running/Deploying builds as Interrupted, and archives the real `~/.shipright/builds` to `builds.migrated`. Isolate the legacy data path (or register the desktop stores with the resolved profile data dir) so a smoke run is fully contained in its temp dir.
findings.evidence: main() isolates only SHIPRIGHT_DATA_DIR/--data-dir to a temp dir (run.mjs:66-76, 230-239), but the desktop stores the started app registers do not all receive it: Program.cs:276 registers `AddSingleton<IBuildStore, SqliteBuildStore>()`, so SqliteBuildStore falls back to `DataDirectory.Resolve()` = `<UserProfile>/.shipright` (SqliteBuildStore.cs:26, DataDirectory.cs:8-16). Observed while running `node scripts/smoke/run.mjs` and a minimal probe: the app logged `Archived builds/ -> C:\Users\nying\.shipright\builds.migrated` and `~/.shipright/builds.migrated` was created (SqliteBuildStore.cs:231-300 runs unconditionally when the real builds dir exists); Program.cs:231 then calls IBuildStore.MarkInterruptedAsync(), which UPDATEs the real `~/.shipright/builds.db` (SqliteBuildStore.cs:126-159).
findings.note: Program.cs:276 now registers `AddSingleton<IBuildStore>(_ => new SqliteBuildStore(dataDir))` (was `AddSingleton<IBuildStore, SqliteBuildStore>()`, whose parameterless ctor fell back to DataDirectory.Resolve() per SqliteBuildStore.cs:26); IServerStore takes dataDir at Program.cs:301 and the five SQLite resource stores at Program.cs:314-318. The stores that AddSchedulerModule/AddWatchBranchModule still build from DataDirectory.Resolve() are overridden with dataDir immediately after those calls (Program.cs:309-313: SqliteBackupHistoryStore, SqliteBackupOverflowStore, SqliteWatchBranchHistoryStore). New proof test DesktopMode_KeepsEveryStoreInsideTheConfiguredDataDirectory asserts projects.db, builds.db, scheduler/backup-history.db and watch-branch/watch-branch.db exist under SHIPRIGHT_DATA_DIR (DesktopModeStartupTests.cs:75-91). The concrete mutations REV-1 documented (real ~/.shipright/builds.db UPDATE via MarkInterruptedAsync, real builds/ archive to builds.migrated) are therefore confined to the temp data dir. The developer additionally reports a real smoke run left ~/.shipright byte-identical.

findings.description: Unbounded in-memory accumulation while only the final 20 lines are used. A chatty or looping server grows this array without limit. Keep a fixed-size ring buffer (or drop all but the last N lines as they arrive).
findings.evidence: capture() does `output.push(line.trimEnd())` for every stdout/stderr line with no cap (run.mjs:251-256); the buffer is only ever consumed by tail(output) which prints the last 20 lines (run.mjs:223-225, 279-282).
findings.note: run.mjs now captures stdout/stderr through a fixed-size ring buffer: createLineBuffer(maxLines = 200) stores at most 200 lines (run.mjs:227-244), capture() pushes into it via `output.push(...)` (run.mjs:274-279), and tail() reads `buffer.toArray().slice(-max)` (run.mjs:246-248, 302). Memory no longer grows with server chatter. A unit test, 'createLineBuffer keeps only the most recent lines in bounded memory', pushes 10 lines into a 3-line buffer and asserts only line-8..line-10 remain (run.test.mjs:209-216).

findings.description: The home-page check can pass on a placeholder the runner itself supplied, so a build with no real home page would still report PASS. This weakens the start-up proof R11 asks for; fail instead when the app's own home page is missing. (Intentional per the design's staging note, hence advisory.)
findings.evidence: resolveContentRoot writes a synthetic `<!doctype html>...` index.html when neither the project wwwroot nor front-end/out exists (run.mjs:124-133); MapFallbackToFile then serves it, so checkHomePage() (run.mjs:178-184, invoked at 266-267) sees 200 text/html even though the app's real home page is absent.

findings.description: A timer is left pending (up to 5s) after the process it guards has already exited; clear it on the exit path (or unref it). Low impact today because main()'s wrapper exits the process immediately afterwards.
findings.evidence: stopServer() creates `setTimeout(() => resolveExit(false), timeoutMs)` and never clears it when the child's exit fires first (run.mjs:205-208).

findings.note: run.test.mjs:218-234 adds 'R11 the runner leaves no app process running and keeps all data in a temp dir it removes', run for both the pass ('ok') and a failure ('badhome') mode. findings.description: A read-only Viewer (or Operator) can fetch the company's Docker registry credentials, including the plaintext password, by calling GET /api/resources/registries or /api/resources/registries/{id}. Sensitive columns must not be returned; the server (not the UI) is the authority per R5. Return a DTO without Password (as team/password responses do) and/or raise the read rule to Admin like credentials.
findings.evidence: MapGet("/api/resources/registries") returns store.GetAllAsync() (and /{id} at line 20), so every DockerRegistryResource crosses the HTTP boundary including its plaintext Password field (Models/DockerRegistryResource.cs:15). RoleAccessRules.cs:28 assigns any other GET under /api/resources only AppRoles.Viewer, so an Operator or Viewer in the same company receives the registry password in the JSON response. Only GET /api/resources/credentials is Admin-restricted (RoleAccessRules.cs:26) even though registries carry the same class of secret; writes are Admin (RoleAccessRules.cs:29) but reads are not.
findings.note: RoleAccessRules.cs:28 now reads `R("GET", @"/api/resources/registries(/.*)?", AppRoles.Admin)`, so both GET /api/resources/registries and /{id} are Admin-only (first matching rule wins; line 30 still covers only the remaining /api/resources GETs as Viewer). RoleAuthorizationHandler runs as the fallback policy for every route ResourceRouter maps (IdentityRegistration.cs:80-82, Program.cs:165-167), so a Viewer/Operator is refused before the handler returns the record. Verified by running the targeted suite `dotnet test --filter FullyQualifiedName~RoleAccessRulesTests`: 46 passed / 0 failed, including SecretBearingResourceReads_NeedAdmin which asserts Admin for /api/resources/registries and /api/resources/registries/abc. This is the finding's 'or raise the read rule to Admin like credentials' option.

findings.description: A Viewer or Operator can read the company's AWS secret access keys and session tokens from GET /api/resources/aws-profiles and /api/resources/aws-profiles/{id}. This exposes usable long-lived cloud credentials to the lowest role. Exclude SecretAccessKey/SessionToken from the response (return a DTO) and restrict the read to Admin, or mark the fields write-only.
findings.evidence: MapGet("/api/resources/aws-profiles") returns store.GetAllAsync() (and /{id} at line 218), so every AwsProfileResource crosses the HTTP boundary including SecretAccessKey and SessionToken (Models/AwsProfileResource.cs:15-16). RoleAccessRules.cs:28 assigns this GET only AppRoles.Viewer. The nearby GET /api/resources/aws-profiles/available is deliberately Admin-only (RoleAccessRules.cs:27), which shows secret-bearing AWS reads are meant to be Admin; the list and detail endpoints were missed.
findings.note: RoleAccessRules.cs:29 now reads `R("GET", @"/api/resources/aws-profiles(/.*)?", AppRoles.Admin)`, which covers the list, /{id} and the previously Admin-only /available route, so SecretAccessKey and SessionToken (AwsProfileResource.cs:15-16) no longer reach a Viewer or Operator. Same fallback-policy enforcement and same passing RoleAccessRulesTests run as SEC-1 (SecretBearingResourceReads_NeedAdmin asserts Admin for /api/resources/aws-profiles and /api/resources/aws-profiles/abc while /api/resources/scripts stays Viewer). This is the finding's 'restrict the read to Admin' option.

findings.description: Same root cause as the registry and AWS findings: whole resource records (with their Variables maps) are returned to any signed-in role. If Variables can hold secrets, scrub them from read responses or require Admin.
findings.evidence: GET /api/resources/scripts (line 74) and GET /api/resources/pipelines (PipelineRouter.cs:13) return ScriptResource/PipelineResource directly, including the Variables dictionary (Models/ScriptResource.cs:13, Models/PipelineResource.cs:12) which holds arbitrary environment values that frequently contain tokens/secrets. Both are Viewer-readable under RoleAccessRules.cs:28.

findings.description: In the standard docker-compose / reverse-proxy deployment the 7-day session cookie can be sent over the local hop in cleartext. Set CookieSecurePolicy.Always in cloud mode (or configure forwarded headers before production).
findings.evidence: options.Cookie.SecurePolicy = CookieSecurePolicy.SameAsRequest with isPersistent:true and a 7-day ExpireTimeSpan (IdentityRegistration.cs:74). Program.cs calls neither UseForwardedHeaders nor UseHttpsRedirection (Program.cs:151-168), so a TLS-terminating proxy that forwards plain HTTP yields a session cookie with no Secure attribute.

findings.description: The switch from bearer headers to a cookie session adds CSRF exposure that no token check covers. SameSite=Strict for the auth cookie and/or antiforgery validation on /api mutations would close it, and mutating GETs should not be GET.
findings.evidence: SameSite=Lax is the only anti-CSRF defence; there is no antiforgery token anywhere in ShipRight.Server or front-end/src/shared (grep for antiforgery/csrf/xsrf/X-CSRF finds nothing). State-changing GETs exist: DatabaseRouter.cs:245 and ServerRouter.cs:373 /db/backups/open-folder perform a host-side action, and SameSite=Lax attaches the cookie on a top-level cross-site navigation to them.

findings.description: A single client can exhaust the shared reset/login budget and block sign-in and password resets for every tenant, weakening R10's reset-rate limit. Configure trusted forwarded headers (X-Forwarded-For) or partition on a stable client identity.
findings.evidence: Every limiter partitions on context.Connection.RemoteIpAddress (lines 48-74), and no forwarded-header middleware runs (Program.cs:151-168). Behind a reverse proxy all requests share the proxy IP, collapsing the global 100/min, the 30/min AuthAttempts and the 5/hour PasswordReset partitions into one site-wide bucket.

findings.description: Server-targeted deploy is Admin-only while build deploy is Operator. If standalone-server deploy counts as 'deploy' per R5 the role table is wrong; if it is intended to be Admin it should be an explicit, commented rule rather than an accidental catch-all. Over-restriction, so advisory rather than a vulnerability.
findings.evidence: POST /api/servers/{serverId}/deploy (ServerBootstrapRouter.cs:27) is not in the Operator allow-list (RoleAccessRules.cs:35) and falls through to the Admin catch-all at line 37, whereas POST /api/builds/{id}/deploy requires only Operator. R5 says an Operator can build and deploy.

findings.description: Unauthenticated information disclosure of the host data-directory path and record counts. Low impact and required by R11's readiness probe, but consider dropping the path/counts from the public payload.
findings.evidence: Public GET /api/health returns DataDirectory (absolute server path), ProjectCount, BuildCount, server/web versions and StartedAt (HealthPayload lines 12-21). RoleAccessRules.cs:63 keeps it anonymous so the smoke runner can probe it.

findings.description: Minor unbounded-work risk in the new smoke runner: cap the captured buffer (ring buffer / max N lines) the way `tail` already caps what is printed. Not reachable by an attacker, so advisory.
findings.evidence: The capture handler pushes every stdout/stderr line into the unbounded `output` array (lines 251-259) with no cap, while only the last 20 are printed. A server that logs heavily during the up-to-60s readiness wait can grow this without limit.

findings.description: Residual to REV-1, not a repeat of it: the file-mutating behaviour REV-1 proved (real builds.db UPDATE and real builds/ archive) is gone, but one desktop store still resolves the legacy ~/.shipright path. It contradicts the claim that every desktop store is registered with the resolved profile data directory, and on a clean machine a smoke run would create real (empty) directories under the user profile. Advisory because no existing data file is changed and R11's edge case names data and project files.
findings.evidence: Program.cs:279 still registers `services.AddSingleton<KnownHostsStore>()` with no resolved dataDir, so KnownHostsStore's ctor uses the legacy path: `_path = Path.Combine(DataDirectory.Resolve(), "known_hosts")` (KnownHostsStore.cs:16-19), and `DataDirectory.Resolve()` calls `EnsureSubdirectories`, which creates builds/, logs/, backups/, scheduler/ and scheduler/overflow/ under <UserProfile>/.shipright (DataDirectory.cs:8-16, 25-32). DatabaseOrchestrator (ctor dependency, DatabaseOrchestrator.cs:30-34) is resolved at start-up by the scheduler queue factory (`sp.GetRequiredService<Database.DatabaseOrchestrator>()`, SchedulerModule.cs:23-24) when the hosted service starts, so this legacy path is resolved on every desktop/smoke start. On a machine where ~/.shipright does not exist yet this creates it (empty directories); the developer's byte-identical check ran on a machine where it already existed, so it could not observe this.

findings.description: R9 edge case 'A very long name or email does not break the layout' now has a test that names R9 and protects the wrapping class; the assertion covers the class application rather than the CSS rule, which is a stronger-assertion gap, not a missing test.
findings.evidence: The new test renders a 200-char name and a 190-char email and asserts each span carries styles.cellText (lines 104-107), the guard class that TeamPage.tsx:140,145 applies and TeamPage.module.css:114-118 wraps. This is the strongest check jsdom can make (it cannot compute layout), but it would not fail if only the .cellText word-break/overflow-wrap rule in the CSS were deleted, because jest maps CSS modules to a name proxy (styles.cellText === 'cellText'). Residual proof-strength gap only.

findings.description: Same class as the fixed SEC-1/SEC-2: the new Viewer/Operator roles can fetch plaintext credentials the moment they can read a project. GET /api/projects and GET /api/projects/{id} must not return DockerPassword or database RootPassword to non-Admin callers - return a DTO without those fields (blank them for non-Admin, as the team/password responses do), since Viewer must still list projects per R5.
findings.evidence: GET /api/projects returns `Results.Ok(await store.GetAllAsync())` and GET /api/projects/{id} (lines 33-39) returns the project directly; the cloud store (CloudDiRegistrar.cs:78 -> CompanyScopedProjectStore) deserializes ProjectConfig straight from the Data column, and MariadbProjectStore.cs:84/98 writes that JSON with no encryption (unlike JsonProjectStore/SqliteProjectStore which encrypt at rest). ProjectConfig carries public serialized secrets: ProjectConfig.cs:48 DockerPassword (ServiceConfig) and ProjectConfig.cs:18 RootPassword (DatabaseConfig). RoleAccessRules.cs has no specific /api/projects GET rule, so the default at line 73 assigns it Viewer (also asserted by RoleAccessRulesTests.cs:31), meaning any Viewer or Operator receives the company's Docker registry password and database root password in plaintext.
findings.note: Both project read endpoints now bind ClaimsPrincipal and run the result through RedactCredentialsFor: GET /api/projects at ProjectRouter.cs:18-19 and GET /api/projects/{id} at ProjectRouter.cs:35-41, calling the new helper at lines 170-181. The helper returns ProjectConfig unchanged only when the caller is unauthenticated (desktop/local, which binds 127.0.0.1 per Program.cs:81) or in AppRoles.Admin; for any other authenticated caller it returns a copy with every ServiceConfig.DockerPassword and DatabaseConfig.RootPassword set to empty, while the project itself (name, services, image names) is still returned. The role claim is ClaimTypes.Role (AppClaimsPrincipalFactory.cs:20), so user.IsInRole(AppRoles.Admin) evaluates correctly, and RoleAccessRules.cs:30 keeps the GETs at Viewer so a Viewer can still list projects per R5. Evidence of the outcome: CloudApiPipelineTests.cs:667 ProjectReads_GiveEveryRoleTheList_ButOnlyAnAdminTheStoredPasswords seeds a project whose JSON contains dockerPassword 'd0cker-secret-pass' and rootPassword 'r00t-secret-pass' and asserts Viewer and Operator get HTTP 200 with 'ghcr.io/org/api' but never either password, and an Admin receives both; the developer reports the full suite at 911 passed / 0 failed with this new test. The company-scoped store is untouched, so BuildOrchestrator/ResourceResolutionService still see the plaintext internally.

findings.description: The developer's round-2 fix raised registries and aws-profiles reads to Admin but scripts and pipelines - same root cause, whole record returned - are still Viewer-readable. If Variables can hold secrets, scrub them from non-Admin read responses or raise those reads to Admin.
findings.evidence: GET /api/resources/scripts (ResourceRouter.cs:74-78) returns ScriptResource whole and PipelineRouter.cs:13-35 returns PipelineResource whole, both including the Variables map (ScriptResource.cs:13, PipelineResource.cs:12). Variables feed script execution and are injected as process environment variables (ProcessRunner.cs:108-112, BuildOrchestrator.cs:1306), so they commonly hold tokens and passwords. RoleAccessRules.cs:30 leaves both GETs at Viewer.

findings.description: Set CookieSecurePolicy.Always in cloud mode (or run forwarded-headers middleware before authentication) so the session cookie is never sent in cleartext. Unchanged from the round-1 advisory, still open.
findings.evidence: options.Cookie.SecurePolicy = CookieSecurePolicy.SameAsRequest with a 7-day session; Program.cs (lines 151-168) calls neither UseForwardedHeaders nor UseHttpsRedirection, so behind the docker-compose TLS-terminating proxy the auth cookie is issued without the Secure attribute and can travel over the plain-HTTP hop.

findings.description: Add antiforgery validation on /api mutations and/or SameSite=Strict for the auth cookie, and stop modelling host actions as GET. Unchanged from the round-1 advisory, still open.
findings.evidence: SameSite=Lax is the only anti-CSRF defence and no antiforgery token exists anywhere in ShipRight.Server or front-end/src/shared. The switch from bearer headers to a cookie session therefore introduces CSRF exposure on state-changing calls, and mutating GETs (DatabaseRouter.cs:245, ServerRouter.cs:373 open-folder/backups) are reachable by a top-level cross-site navigation under Lax.

findings.description: SEC-10's fix covers the two named credential fields, but the same whole-ProjectConfig response still carries ServerConfig.EnvFile - the remote .env contents - to non-Admin callers. Blank EnvFile for authenticated non-Admins as well (or return a role-shaped DTO). Recorded advisory rather than blocking because EnvFile is user-supplied config text, not one of the named sensitive columns in API-004.
findings.evidence: RedactCredentialsFor (ProjectRouter.cs:170-181) blanks only ServiceConfig.DockerPassword and DatabaseConfig.RootPassword. ProjectConfig.Server.EnvFile (ProjectConfig.cs:135) is described as 'Full contents of the .env file written to RemoteWorkingDir' and is written verbatim to the server by RemoteServerBootstrapper.cs:111-112 and RemoteServerDeployer.cs:74-77 via RemoteEnvFileWriter, so it routinely holds database/API secrets. GET /api/projects and GET /api/projects/{id} (RoleAccessRules.cs:30 leaves these GETs at Viewer) still return that ServerConfig whole, so a Viewer or Operator receives whatever secrets the .env body contains.
